desktop.notes:
• Send to Curish (right-click, replaces Send to RapidRAW): opens the photo in Curish, in its folder, ready to edit. An open Curish is reused; a photo not in the Library yet is sent first.
• Jump through big folders: Page Up / Page Down, or hold F and turn the mouse wheel, jumps 25 photos (Settings → General). Home / End = first / last photo shown. Only the photo you land on loads.
• F = Favourite, one star even on a long press. Alt+F adds the selection to the album you used last (asks the first time).
• Crop: dragging next to the frame turns the frame over a still photo (with a grid); hold E to turn the photo instead. The shape label stays on the frame.
• Free crop suggests the nearest standard shape (≈ 3:2, 4:3, 16:9, 1:1, portrait too): click to set it exactly, still free. Green ✓ = an exact match. Dragging a frame into the photo's edge slides along it instead of sticking.
• Duplicate Photo (right-click): a copy next to it (RAW + JPEG together, same quality and EXIF), selected.
• Culling dashboard (Tools): your sessions - keep / discard / favourite, undo and changed decisions, compares, how often you go with the AI, album additions, time per decision and photos per minute (idle time not counted).
• My AI preferences (Settings → Learning): tick what you like (close-ups, action, interaction, unusual moments…) or write it; the AI leans that way. Suggestions only - nothing is decided or deleted.
• Viewer strip: clicking a thumbnail always selects that photo (it used to slide and pick its neighbour).
• Big folders are faster: with a camera or tag filter on, deciding a photo no longer freezes a 6,000-photo folder.
